target_customer: Large US health systems such as Cleveland Clinic
problem: Health system staff spend time on manual cross-system tasks (referral intake, registration, denials) that rigid RPA cannot handle.
business_model: Enterprise software contracts for automation platform
product_category: AI workflow automation for healthcare operations

founders.name: Kesava Kirupa Dinakaran
founders.background_notes: YC page lists him as CEO and founder. TechCrunch says the founders lived in a San Francisco hacker house and paid bills winning hackathons.

technical_complexity.rationale: Browser and desktop automation with machine learning is standard but brittle; healthcare compliance adds work.

defensibility.rationale: Deep integrations inside health systems create switching costs; underlying automation could be matched by RPA vendors.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Press contrasts Luminai with legacy RPA. No source shows incumbents copying it; incumbents were not sourced as named competitors.

market_need_then: Health systems carry heavy manual administrative load; Cleveland Clinic became a named customer by 2026.

identity.logo: Logo and icon, design not described

rebrands.why: Not stated; announced with the Series A

brand_strength.rationale: Rename to a distinctive coined name improved on a generic one, but no brand press or community found.

pivots.from: DigitalBrain, enhancing helpdesks to speed support tickets (per a secondary profile)
pivots.to: AI platform for health system operations

outcome_analysis: DigitalBrain won a $3.4M seed after YC, renamed to Luminai with a $16M General Catalyst led Series A in June 2022, then focused on healthcare and landed Cleveland Clinic. A $38M Series B in April 2026 brought total raised to $60M, which the company confirms. Success came from a vertical focus and enterprise sales.
notes: Series A lead conflict: one ZoomInfo page names Craft Ventures; TechCrunch and others say General Catalyst. Series A date 2022-06-09 per TechCrunch; an aggregator says April. Seed date not given by TechCrunch (a secondary profile says October 2020). Total of about $60M agrees with the YC page description. Co-founder Dmitry Dolgopolov appears only in secondary profiles, not listed. No competitor with a source dated near 2020 found. Downgraded to depth 1 by orchestrator: the researcher reported that the branding search was shared with other searches.
